analysis.title: Sunday Start | Who's Afraid of the Big Blue Wave?
key_insights: Andrew Sheets argues the recent historic drawdowns in cyclicals and momentum factors are more likely a near-bottom clearing event than an end-of-cycle signal.

Cycle indicators do not confirm an end-of-cycle story: manufacturing PMIs remain strong globally (US print better than expected on Monday), the US leading economic indicators index is improving, bank loan growth in the US, Europe and Asia is rising, and credit fundamentals are improving.

Friday's US jobs report showed payrolls surging with no serious signs of overheating. The Cross-Asset team's Cycle Model still looks healthy, and its US market cycle framework signals 'Mature Advance'.
Yield curves (2s10s and 3m10y) remain positively sloped in the US, UK, Germany and Japan. This is not the signal expected if policy were excessively tight and growth about to roll over.
Morgan Stanley's global growth forecasts for the next 6-12 months remain solid, with growth over 2% in the US and over 1% in Europe.

Tuesday's midterms produced a 'Blue Wave', the strongest Democratic nationwide-vote outperformance since 1974. Democrats flipped the House, the Senate and several governorships, including Texas and Ohio. The concern is that more regulation could slow the AI buildout. MS says this is possible but not its base case.

Semiconductor stocks were already down 30% from their June peak before Tuesday. Even in the high-constraints bear case with tougher permitting and power, MS still sees a +17% pa CAGR in global data center capacity to 2030.

The S&P 500 forward P/E has de-rated about 19% YTD. The strategist argues markets can finish adjusting well before the uncertainty is resolved, and that Equity Strategists see this adjustment having run under the surface for some time.

For fixed income, the midterms may ease two concerns: high energy prices and heavy borrowing to finance data centres. A slower, more prolonged AI buildout spreads borrowing over more years, which is good for credit.

Voter unease with the Iran conflict, cited by the Vice President as a factor in the results, could lower the market's perceived risk of re-escalation. Oil is 17% below its end-October level. Lower oil is especially relevant in Europe, where rate strategists favour curve steepeners, and helps EM on several fronts.

Broader voter discontent with inflation could reinforce expectations that tariffs will prove temporary. Larger Democratic majorities could reduce the influence of individual holdouts in Congress and remove one source of volatility.
Conclusion: a clearing event for key uncertainties is more likely than a real cycle turn. MS will keep testing the view against the evidence.

tension_points.bull_case: Even in a high-constraints scenario global data center capacity still grows at a +17% pa CAGR to 2030. Semis are already down 30% from their June peak and the S&P 500 forward P/E has de-rated about 19% YTD, so much of the adjustment is priced. A slower buildout is good for credit.
tension_points.bear_case: The Blue Wave and state-level Democratic gains could bring more regulation that significantly slows the AI buildout.

tension_points.theme: End of cycle versus clearing event
tension_points.bull_case: Manufacturing PMIs are strong, the leading indicators index is improving, loan growth is rising, yield curves are positively sloped, and the Cycle Model reads 'Mature Advance'. The factor drawdowns are a clearing event.
tension_points.bear_case: Historic drawdowns in cyclicals and momentum are the type of price action usually seen at the end of an economic cycle, and yields may be too high for the economy to handle.

theme_stances.key_argument: Cycle data remain encouraging and the midterm result may ease two of the bond market's biggest concerns, so a clearing event is more likely than a cycle turn.
theme_stances.evidence: We think the latter is much more likely.

theme_stances.key_argument: Midterms may ease high energy prices and heavy data-center borrowing, the two storm clouds over bond markets this year.
theme_stances.evidence: the midterms ease concerns around both.
